ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a nitrogen-containing six-membered ring; the nitrogen on the ring is also connected to a methyl group and an N–O bond; on the right side is an anhydride structure containing two CF3 groups, with two carbonyl C=O groups, and connecting two acyl groups through a middle oxygen. There are also reaction arrows and electron movement arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: Counting according to the specified method, in the left component the six-membered ring has 6 heavy-atom bonds, the N–O bond is 1, and the N–methyl bond is 1, for a total of 8. In the anhydride on the right, the two CF3 groups together have 6 C–F bonds, and each is connected to a carbonyl carbon to form 2 C–C bonds; the two carbonyl C=O count as 2 bonds; the bonds between the two acyl carbons and the bridging oxygen count as 2 bonds. Therefore the anhydride part has a total of 6 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 12 bonds. The total number is 8 + 12 = 20.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First count the left component: the six-membered ring contributes 6 heavy-atom bonds, the N–O bond contributes 1, and the N–methyl bond contributes 1, giving 8. Then count the anhydride: two CF3 groups contribute 6 C–F bonds plus 2 C–carbonyl bonds; the two carbonyl C=O bonds contribute 2; and the two acyl–O bonds to the bridging oxygen contribute 2, giving 12. Add the components: 8 + 12 = 20.
